newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - Set to firm except fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - Set to firm except fuel oil.

text.p: European oil products look set for a firm week, except for fuel oil which faces an uncertain future after recent price volatility, traders said.

Gas oil's prospects will depend largely on the continuation of the arbitrage to the East while gasoline may firm on expectations of increased demand into May. Naphtha could also encounter improved end-user interest.
Gas oil traders have become increasingly wary about the arb's life expectancy.
"It's definitely been narrowing and I think freight is too expensive," said one trader.
With Northwest European fob cargoes pegged around $162 a tonne, Singapore fob cargoes at $194 tonne and freight on 60,000 tonne cargoes at $30 a tonne, the arb appeared still narrowly open.
Diesel looks set to hold on to strong premiums this week on the back of tight supplies. Traders said demand was not excessive, but it was outpacing supply.
"The expectation is of it getting stronger," said one dealer who said May IPE +$15 cif NWE may be achieved.
Heating oil should hold steady with FOD and DIN premiums hovering around May IPE +$4-5 cif level.
Gasoline was expected to firm into May.

"I don't expect the situation to change that drastically over the coming week but May delivery material should firm," said one trader. Eurograde May barges were pegged at $198 while April was talked at $194-195.
Traders estimated some 100,000 tonnes of material was being held in storage in ARA, and some suggested a couple of players could be planning a squeeze on the region.
"I don't think it can be pulled off especially with so little material being moved over to the U.S," one trader said.
Naphtha was also expected to strengthen with more end-user buying interest emerging, although some traders said supplies could increase if Sonatrach stood by its decision to bar double stem loading.
The move could dissuade some players from moving material Eastwards due to the lower returns on shipping smaller parcel, traders said.
Price levels for full-range naphtha cargoes were assessed at around $173/$175 cif NWE on Friday.

Fuel oil will continue with its uncertain tone. After last week's volatility and thin trade players were cautious about predicting a direction. Many saw prices continuing to swing up and down in a narrow range above $80, buffeted by manipulation.
Low sulphur should continue moribund both in the north and in the Mediterranean, with the big Italian buyer keeping prices well clamped down below $98 cif Med.
High sulphur will continue long in the Med, with buying weak and the supply picture confused. Traders were watching for one large cargo to head to Asia.

Life has returned to straight-run and Russian feedstock markets after crude recovered from lows, making processing residues more profitable. U.S buyers may pick up the European straight-run cargoes still left in May, traders say.
